title: Unified scoring proxy for quantization calibration and validation
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Motivation: Calibration runs for FP8/INT8 quant profiles produce large candidate sets but our current scoring is fragmented: separate scripts for perplexity, task suites (MMLU-style), and text-similarity metrics (ROUGE/BLEU), plus bespoke task scorers. This ticket builds a unified scoring proxy (USProxy) that standardizes metric contracts, supports streaming evaluation during calibration, and emits normalized scores to the Console and the calibration pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: USProxy accepts a standard evaluation job payload (model variant, dataset id, metric set) and returns a JSON lines stream of scores or an aggregated report
Supports core metrics: perplexity (batch and streaming), MMLU-style accuracy/EM, Rouge-L and BLEU for generation tasks, and an SDK hook for task-specific scorers (e.g., QA F1, NER span-F1)
Implements score normalization rules and uncertainty estimates (bootstrap CI) and stores raw & normalized scores to the Eval DB and Console under runtime-1.20 release
Calibration pipeline can call USProxy as a blocking quality gate and fail a quant profile when normalized score drops > configured threshold versus baseline
Unit/integration tests covering metric correctness against small reference datasets and synthetic cases
Performance: streaming throughput at 200 evals/sec for lightweight metrics or <10ms per eval when using cached embeddings; cold-latency for complex scorers <200ms per sample on CI hardware baseline
Documentation: public API contract, example payloads, migration notes for older scripts, and runbook for troubleshooting
implementation_notes: Design a thin HTTP/gRPC proxy that dispatches to metric backends (native Rust scoring libs for perplexity; PyTorch/Python for task scorers) to avoid shipping heavy Python into the runtime path

Define a stable metric schema: {metric_name, task_type, directionality (higher_better), numeric_range, aggregation_method, confidence_interval} — transported as top-level fields in the response (strings or numeric arrays serialized as strings)
Support two modes: streaming (score lines emitted as samples are processed) and batch (single aggregated report). Calibration jobs should default to streaming to allow early failure and cache warm-up

Normalization: use baseline profiles stored in Eval DB and apply a configurable mapping (absolute delta, percent, or z-score) per metric. Defaults: perplexity => lower better (relative change), MMLU => absolute accuracy delta, Rouge/BLEU => percent change
Bootstrap CI: implement 1k-sample bootstrap by default with configurable seed and sample size; expose CI as part of gate decision

Task scorer SDK: small Python package with a narrow shim interface (score(batch_predictions, batch_references, params) -> list[score]) and a registration mechanism with USProxy. Include example QA and NER scorers
Caching: integrate with the calibration cache to reuse tokenized inputs and embeddings; for generation metrics store reference embeddings keyed by dataset+model+prompt-hash
Cost trade-offs: heavy scorers run on a worker pool (spot/GPU) and return results to proxy; lightweight scorers run inline. Provide controls for evaluator cost limits per job
Metrics telemetry: emit internal latency, error-rate, and resource-usage events to tracing and to Console per-eval breakdown
test_plan: Unit tests for each metric backend comparing against canonical implementations (sacreBLEU for BLEU, rouge_score for ROUGE) using small fixture datasets
Integration test: run a small quant calibration with 3 candidate profiles and assert USProxy provides consistent gates and that the calibration pipeline respects gating decisions
Golden tests: record normalized scores for a baseline model+dataset and alert on drift when refactoring scoring code
Load test: simulate 5k concurrent small eval jobs to validate streaming throughput and worker autoscaling behavior
Failure mode tests: backend timeouts, incomplete metric results, and partial streaming — ensure graceful degradation and clear error codes
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): Deploy USProxy behind feature flag and route 5% of new calibration jobs; monitor Console for score parity vs legacy scripts
Stage 2 (wider rollout): 50% of calibration traffic, validate bootstrap CI stability, and run reconciliation jobs to backfill Eval DB
Stage 3 (cutover): Switch default calibration pipeline to call USProxy and deprecate legacy scoring scripts after 2 weeks of parity
Fallback: calibration pipeline maintains toggle to run legacy scorer in shadow mode and to short-circuit to legacy results if USProxy fails
Migration: provide a one-click job to re-score previous calibration runs with USProxy for auditability
